memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the whole Israelite community withdrew from Moses' presence, and everyone who was willing and whose heart moved them came and brought an offering to the Lord for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the sacred garments." - Exod 35:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They heard, they went home, and then they came back carrying things.

That gap between hearing and returning is where most of our good intentions die. We are moved in a service, we mean to respond, and then ordinary life closes over the moment. Israel actually came back.

Notice what drove them: "whose heart moved them." This was not organised pressure. Something inside them stirred, and they acted on it before it faded.

That stirring is God's own work. Paul says it is God who works in us to will and to act in order to fulfil His good purpose (Phil 2:13). When you feel prompted to give, forgive, serve or speak, that impulse did not begin with you.

But it can be ignored. James warns against being hearers who merely listen and deceive themselves — the doing is what matters (Jas 1:22).

So here is a practical test. What has God stirred in you recently that you have not yet acted on? A conversation you know you should have. A gift you meant to give. A habit you meant to end. A person you meant to call.

Do not let it die in the gap between hearing and going home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God stirred in you that you have not acted on?
2. Why do good intentions so often fade before they become action?
3. What is one thing you could do today rather than later?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for stirring my heart. Help me act on it before the moment passes. Amen.
